ACT · STUDY GUIDE

Information Technology Act, 2000

The central technology-specific statute: electronic governance, security, cyber offences, state powers, intermediary liability, and institutional functions.

2000 · amended through the notified text21 explained sections
Official full textPrint guide
Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015). Old compilations may still print it. The BNS did not repeal the IT Act.

Understand the provision.

Original plain-language explanations. The official text controls.

IT Act · 1

Extent and extraterritorial application

Read with section 75. The Act extends to the whole of India and, in specified circumstances, to offences or contraventions outside India involving a computer, system, or network located in India. Extraterritorial reach is not unlimited enforcement jurisdiction.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 2

Definitions

Defines terms including computer, computer resource, communication device, data, electronic record, intermediary, and secure electronic record. Check the exact clause and amendments before applying a definition; everyday meanings may be narrower or broader.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 4–5

Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures

Provide legal-recognition rules for electronic records and electronic authentication, subject to exclusions and prescribed requirements. Recognition is not a guarantee of authenticity, execution, or admissibility in every dispute.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 7–10A

Retention, government records, and electronic contracts

Address retention, use in government processes, signature-related rules, and contract formation through electronic means. Other statutes and excluded document categories still matter.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 43

Damage to computer systems

Addresses specified acts without permission, including unauthorized access, downloading, introducing contaminants, damage, disruption, denial of access, and assistance, with compensation under the provision. Identify the precise clause and the affected system.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 43A

Sensitive personal data security

Concerns compensation for a body corporate’s negligent failure to maintain reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data it possesses, deals with, or handles, where wrongful loss or gain results. Read with the 2011 SPDI Rules and the DPDP commencement framework.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 65

Tampering with computer source documents

Addresses knowing or intentional concealment, destruction, or alteration of computer source code required to be kept or produced by law. This is not the old Evidence Act section 65 on secondary evidence.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 66

Computer-related offences

Criminalizes dishonest or fraudulent commission of acts referred to in section 43. It is not a general offence of every unauthorized use; the underlying act and required mental element must be established.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 66A

Offensive messages — struck down

The Supreme Court struck down section 66A in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015). Do not present it as a valid current charge merely because it appears in an old bare Act or case template.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 66B–66D

Stolen resources, identity theft, and personation

66B concerns dishonest receipt or retention of stolen computer resources or communication devices; 66C addresses fraudulent or dishonest use of specified identification features; 66D addresses cheating by personation using a computer resource. Distinguish the ingredients.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 66E–66F

Privacy and terrorism

66E addresses specified intentional private-image capture or dissemination without consent. 66F addresses cyber terrorism under defined intent, means, and consequences; not every intrusion or politically motivated post satisfies it.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 67–67C

Electronic publication and preservation offences

67 concerns specified obscene electronic material; 67A sexually explicit material; 67B specified child sexual exploitation material; 67C failure by a person in charge to preserve specified information. Apply exact definitions and sensitive-handling safeguards.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 69

Interception, monitoring, and decryption

Authorizes specified action under the statutory grounds and procedure, including the 2009 Rules. It is distinct from a section 91 production order, a search, and a section 69A blocking direction.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 69A–69B

Blocking and traffic data

69A provides a blocking framework for specified sovereign, security, public-order, and related interests, with procedural safeguards. 69B concerns authorized collection of specified traffic data for cybersecurity functions. Neither is a blanket investigative permission.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 70–70B

Protected systems and national institutions

Section 70 addresses notified protected systems. Sections 70A and 70B concern critical information infrastructure protection and CERT-In functions. Verify current institutional notifications and the exact scope of each role.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 72–72A

Confidentiality and personal-data disclosure

Address specified breaches of confidentiality and disclosure of personal information obtained under contractual or statutory powers. Consent, lawful purpose, and the conditions of the provision must be examined.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 75

Extraterritorial operation

Extends specified application to conduct outside India involving a computer, computer system, or network located in India. Coordinate with procedural law and international cooperation for overseas evidence.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 79

Conditional intermediary safe harbour

Protects qualifying intermediaries in specified circumstances, subject to subsections (2) and (3), applicable Rules, and judicial interpretation. It is not immunity for every act or a substitute for due diligence.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 80–81

Police powers and overriding effect

Section 80 provides specified police powers for offences under the Act. Section 81 gives overriding effect subject to its wording. Neither eliminates constitutional or procedural safeguards.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 87

Power to make rules

Provides the delegated authority under which multiple rule sets are framed. Always identify the particular rule, clause, notification, and amendment rather than citing only “the IT Rules”.

Verify in the official text
IT Act · 94

Short title, extent, and commencement

Contains the Act’s citation, extent, and commencement provisions. For a general production order concerning electronic records, consult BNSS section 94 (formerly CrPC section 91), not a supposed IT Act section 91 production power. The IT Act’s section 91 concerns amendment of the Indian Penal Code.

Verify in the official text
